rootNote: Teaching root chosen from WLC counts (OSHB 3d15126): H1540 גָּלָה has 186 verb tokens (Qal 49, Niphal 32, Piel 56, Pual 2, Hitpael 2, Hiphil 38, Hophal 7) and is the only frequent III-He root with no second weakness that is attested in all seven stems. It is the paradigm root of GKC §75 / Paradigm P and Davidson §44. בָּנָה (374; Qal, Niphal), שָׁתָה (217; Qal, Niphal) and כָּלָה (203; Qal, Piel, Pual) are more frequent but cover only 2-3 stems. Squares גלה does not attest take examples from other III-He roots. III-He here means a final ה without mappiq (originally י or ו); a final הּ (גָּבַהּ) belongs to III-Guttural.
source: Forms from GKC §75 + Paradigm P (Weak Verbs ל״ה, PDF pp. 484-485) and Davidson, Introductory Hebrew Grammar §44 paradigm (pp. 184-185), both in /workspace/hebrew-books/ and read from page images; GKC §75's text decides ī/ē before consonantal afformatives where Paradigm P's glyphs are unreadable. Squares those books do not print but K&J, Learning Biblical Hebrew pt. 2, III-Waw/Yod chart (pp. 324-325) prints are formBasis 'printed' (tutor ruling 2026-11-21). Remaining squares follow GKC applied to the strong-verb.json pattern (formBasis 'rule'). Endings (ָה, ֶה, ֵה, ֹה, וֹת) and apocopated forms are written exactly as WLC writes them. Not copied from any copyrighted chart.
verificationMethod: Each form was matched (consonants + vowel points, accents ignored, dagesh lene and plene/defective ḥolem, shureq and ḥireq-yod spellings normalized) against OSHB morphhb-wlc tokens with the same OSHB morph slot (jussive squares: OSHB jussive tag). R1 and R2 are positional (ג, ל); everything after R2 (the ה/י/ו of the ending, וֹת, or nothing in apocopated forms) must agree letter for letter; a begadkefat radical's dagesh in dagesh-lene position is optional; Hitpael is matched with and without sibilant metathesis. The example's root was checked against the Strong's headword for its lemma number: it must end in ה without mappiq; 1st radical not guttural/נ/י/ו; 2nd radical not guttural/ר/ו/י (so עשׂה, היה, ראה, נטה, צוה, חיה are never examples). Ketiv excluded. Imperatives may carry paragogic ה; infinitives construct may carry a preposition (examplePrefix). Example preference: teaching root, then another root of the class; each in order no prefix, ו, preposition. Every matched token was cross-checked against STEPBible TAHOT; tokens where TAHOT disagrees are never used as examples.

notes.endings: The ה of III-He verbs is a vowel letter, not a radical: ָה in perfects, ֶה in imperfects and participles, ֵה in imperatives, ֹה in the Qal/Niphal/Piel/Pual infinitive absolute, וֹת in every infinitive construct (GKC §75, law 1). WLC spellings are kept exactly.
notes.originalYod: Before consonantal afformatives the original י reappears as ִי/ֵי (גָּלִיתָ, נִגְלֵיתָ, גֻּלֵּיתָ); before vocalic afformatives it drops (גָּלוּ, תִּגְלִי) (GKC §75, laws 2-3). Only the Qal passive participle keeps it at the end (גָּלוּי).
notes.apocope: Jussive and wayyiqtol drop ֶה (GKC §75, law 5): וַיִּגֶל, וַיִּגָּל, וַיְגַל, וַיִּתְגַּל, וַיֶּגֶל. The wayyiqtol squares use the apocopated form; jussive squares are added for Qal, Niphal, Piel and Hitpael (only where WLC attests them). Pual and Hophal have no shortened forms in the grammars.
notes.cohortative: The ordinary yiqtol with ֶה serves as cohortative (GKC §75, law 6): אֶגְלֶה.
notes.weqatal: וְגָלִיתָ (regular). Shown as a note, not a column.
notes.fsParticiple: III-He feminine participles are -ָה forms (גֹּלָה, נִגְלָה, מְגַלָּה …): GKC §75 law 3, Davidson p. 184, K&J p. 325 and the Bible agree, so the -ֶת main-form ruling has no III-He counterpart.
notes.qalStativeType: Stative III-He verbs (e.g. קָשָׁה, Davidson p. 184) inflect like גָּלָה in the forms here. Note only.
notes.Hophal imperative: None: GKC Paradigm P marks it 'wanting'.
